[T1](../T1-temperature-static/index.qmd) held each bath point until nothing
moved, and every number it produced assumed the sensor had finished
responding. This experiment removes that assumption.

Plunge a sensor from one medium into another and it approaches the new
temperature exponentially, over a time constant set by how fast heat crosses
into it. Measuring that time constant in four media — still air, forced air,
still water, stirred water — separates what belongs to the sensor from what
belongs to the medium, and turns a datasheet's "response time" into a number
with conditions attached.

The result worth carrying away is the **ramp error**: a sensor with time
constant $\tau$ following an input changing at $\dot{T}$ reads low by
$\tau\dot{T}$, permanently, and averaging makes that wrong answer more
confident rather than smaller.

## What you measure {#sec-t2-index-measure}

| Quantity | How | Where it is used later |
|---|---|---|
| Time constant $\tau$, per medium | Nonlinear fit of the step response | Any measurement of a changing temperature |
| Convection coefficient ratios | $h_2/h_1 = \tau_1/\tau_2$ | Choosing a medium, and sizing a probe |
| Ramp dynamic error | Measured, and predicted as $\tau\dot{T}$ | The systematic error a static calibration cannot see |
| Second-order signature | The sheathed probe's inflection | When the lumped model stops applying |

: What T2 produces {#tbl-t2-index-outputs}

## Bench {#sec-t2-index-bench}

**Tier 2.** The [thermal rig](../../hardware/thermal-rig.qmd) and the same two
sensors T1 calibrated, at the same excitation.

**Board.** Any supported board. The fastest medium here needs a few tens of
samples per second, which control transfers alone can supply.

**Host.** Any.

::: {.callout-important}
## This experiment depends on T1's calibration

Volts become temperature through the Steinhart–Hart and Callendar–Van Dusen
curves **fitted in T1**, not from a datasheet. If the sensors have been
re-wired or the excitation changed since, T1 must be repeated first — and T1's
own uncertainty propagates into every time constant measured here, which is
why it appears as a component in the budget.
:::

## Reference data {#sec-t2-index-data}

Six generated runs in `data/`:

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `step-still-air`, `step-forced-air`, `step-still-water`, `step-stirred-water` | Plunge tests, one per medium, each at a rate and duration suited to its own time constant |
| `step-sheathed` | The stirred-water plunge with a sheathed probe — two lumps, not one |
| `ramp-stirred-water` | A steady ramp, for the dynamic error |

: Reference data shipped with T2 {#tbl-t2-index-data}

::: {.content-visible when-profile="instructor"}
## Instructor summary {.instructor-note}

Three hours, tier 2. Still air takes ten minutes per run and cannot be
hurried — start it first and run the faster media while it settles. The two
things worth the discussion time are that $\tau$ belongs to the sensor *and*
the medium, and that the ramp error is systematic. Full notes in the
[handbook](handbook.qmd#sec-t2-instructor).
:::
